practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient instance as a process-wide singleton; do not create a new client per request and only close the client on graceful shutdown.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single, long-lived MongoClient instance (singleton) for the whole Node.js process, reuse it for all operations and only call client.close() on graceful shutdown.

practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable for local/dev usage and never commit it into source control; rotate and deliver secrets via Key Vault or equivalent for production.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code or commit it; rotate secrets via Key Vault or equivalent instead of embedding credentials in repo files.

practices.practice: In Azure-managed environments prefer Azure Key Vault + Managed Identity (and Microsoft Entra identity/RBAC) for credential access instead of using process environment variables directly.
practices.prior_belief: If using Azure-managed services, prefer Azure Key Vault + Managed Identity for credential access instead of process environment variables; fall back to env vars only for local dev with .env.example placeholders.

practices.practice: Always require TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production (ensure tls=true/tls option and a correct CA bundle), addressing CA issues by fixing the cert chain rather than disabling checks.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL in the MongoDB connection string (ssl=true or tls=true) and require certificate validation rather than disabling it, to protect credentials and data in transit.

practices.practice: Tune the driver's connection-pool settings (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, maxIdleTimeMS) to match the application's concurrency profile and follow serverless vs long-running server guidance (small pools for serverless, larger pools for OLTP).
practices.prior_belief: Configure the driver connection pool size (e.g., maxPoolSize) to match expected concurrency and avoid one-client-per-request patterns — keep pool size tuned to the Node.js app's concurrency profile.

practices.practice: Implement robust transient-failure handling: use driver retry features where available, and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff + jitter for transient network errors and respect rate-limit signals (429) and Retry-After headers.
practices.prior_belief: Implement robust transient-failure handling: retry on network errors and transient server errors with exponential backoff + jitter, and handle server throttling (429) specially respecting any Retry-After/x-ms-retry-after headers.

practices.practice: Provision cluster compute/throughput appropriate to vector-search workloads (choose a cluster tier that supports your vector index type and expected vector count, enable autoscale if available, and monitor metrics to increase capacity before throttling occurs).
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput/compute appropriate to vector search workloads (higher RU/s or larger compute tiers) or enable autoscale; monitor consumed RU and increase capacity before throttling becomes common.

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity and store embedding metadata (model name, version, and dimensionality) alongside vectors so you can detect model drift and reindex if models or dimensions change.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding or testing, use deterministic, versioned embeddings and record the embed-model version used; in production ensure embedding model changes are handled via reindexing or model-version fields.

practices.practice: Create a dedicated vector index (cosmosSearch) with explicit parameters (kind, dimensions, similarity, and tuned build/query parameters) that exactly match your embeddings; mismatched dimensions or similarity silently corrupt results.
practices.prior_belief: Create a dedicated vector index with explicit parameters (index type HNSW or DiskANN and tuned parameters like M, efConstruction, efSearch or IVF nlist) appropriate to data size and latency requirements, instead of relying on a default index.

practices.practice: Push cheap metadata predicates into the vector search by using the `filter` parameter in `cosmosSearch` (metadata-first then vector search) rather than post-filtering the kNN results.
practices.prior_belief: Filter by cheap metadata first (e.g., article type, date, client segment) using standard B-tree indexes, then run the vector nearest-neighbors search on the candidate set (metadata-then-vector pattern).

practices.practice: Choose the vector index subtype by scale: prefer DiskANN for production large-scale workloads, HNSW for moderate sizes, and IVF for small collections, because each has different recall/memory/latency trade-offs.
Do not return full vector payloads in normal query responses—project out the vector field and only fetch raw vectors for reindexing or recomputation jobs.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid returning full vector payloads in normal queries — project out vector fields unless you need to compute similarity client-side; only fetch vector data for recomputation or reindexing jobs.

practices.practice: Create conventional B-tree (single-field or compound) indexes on all fields used for equality filters or sorts and declare unique constraints where required to avoid collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create conventional indexes on all fields used for equality or sort filters (e.g., articleId, tenantId, createdAt) and mark any unique keys explicitly (unique: true) to avoid collection scans.

practices.practice: Make index lifecycle operations idempotent: inventory existing indexes (`getIndexes` / `$indexStats`), `hideIndex` to dry-run removals, and only drop indexes after verifying no regressions.
practices.prior_belief: Make index creation idempotent: check existing indexes via listIndexes and only create missing ones; perform index creation during maintenance windows or with throttle controls for large datasets.

practices.practice: Do not store unbounded conversation history in the database; enforce an upper bound via max messages, TTL indexes, or periodic summarization/compaction before persisting agent memory.
practices.prior_belief: Do not store unlimited conversation history in the database unbounded; enforce an upper bound (max messages), TTL, or perform periodic summarization/compaction before saving in-memory agent memory to the DB.

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the BSON size limit: cap document sizes, avoid embedding large transcripts or entire portfolios, and split very large fields into side collections referenced by id.
practices.prior_belief: Cap document sizes and avoid very large single documents (e.g., don't embed excessively large conversation transcripts or entire portfolios), instead store long text as separate documents and reference by id.

practices.practice: Record and version document schema (e.g., add a schemaVersion field) and plan migration/reindexing paths when document shape or embedding dimension changes.
practices.prior_belief: Record and version schema of stored documents (fields, vector dim, metadata) and include migration paths for schema changes and reindexing when vector dimension or metadata shape changes.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and alert on cluster-level saturation (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connection counts) and collect slow-query logs in Log Analytics to find expensive queries; monitor these host-level/IO metrics rather than relying on Cosmos DB-style RU metrics for the managed MongoDB service.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor and log request charge / RU consumption per operation (or equivalent metric) and surface slow queries/expensive vector-search calls so you can tune indexes and partitioning.

practices.practice: For full-text / keyword search use DocumentDB's search indexes created with `createSearchIndexes` and query with the `$search` aggregation stage (BM25, fuzzy, phrase, custom analyzers) rather than MongoDB community `$text` indexes.

Tune vector-index build/query parameters (e.g., maxDegree, lBuild, lSearch, k) and consider product quantization or half-precision indexing to trade memory for recall/latency depending on dataset size and budget.
Make seed scripts idempotent: upsert documents by stable id (or check before insert), and provide a guarded --wipe option for test environments; document the seed behavior.
practices.prior_belief: For local development and automated tests, keep seed scripts idempotent: check for existing documents by stable id and update/skip rather than inserting duplicates; include a --wipe option guarded by clear warnings.

practices.practice: Store vectors in a binary/typed float representation (e.g., Float32 arrays) and keep a documented dimension field so index creation and queries use the correct dimensionality.
practices.prior_belief: When storing vectors, use a typed binary/float representation (Float32 array) rather than JSON strings, and keep a documented 'dimension' field so index creation and retrieval use the correct dimensionality.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector storage binary Float32; "DocumentDB store vectors binary Float32"; "vector storage format DocumentDB"

practices.practice: Avoid deep pagination with large skip values; prefer cursor/range-based pagination (stable sort key like createdAt or _id) to keep queries efficient.
practices.prior_belief: Use pagination (limit + skip or range queries with a stable sort key) for listing results; avoid large skip values for performance — prefer range queries (createdAt, _id) for deep pagination.
practices.how_found: Searches tried: "Azure DocumentDB pagination skip vs range", "avoid large skip Azure DocumentDB", "deep pagination skip performance DocumentDB"
